1134.author: yuanzhou75
1134.body:
Closes #1125


## The defect

A delivered file's revision was registered with `new Date()` sampled *after* the copy, while the file on disk kept its own mtime — and when the bytes already existed, `copyCasToWorkspace({ reuseIdentical: true })` returned before touching the file at all. So the very next workspace listing compared `revision.modifiedAt` against `stat`, found them unequal, appended a revision built by `reconcileWorkspaceFiles`, and moved `currentRevisionId` onto it. That revision carries `origin: "unknown"`, no `contentHash`, no `publicationSequence`, no `artifactVersionIds`, and no `parentRevisionId` — so the provenance view lost the attribution *and* the lineage and the Artifact link, for a file whose bytes never changed.

The observed arrow is arithmetic, not a coincidence: the attributed row's `modifiedAt` is 25 ms *later* than the file's real mtime, which is exactly the clock read.

## The fix

All four clock-stamped registrations now record the file's own `stat.mtime`, matching the paths that already survive a listing (`services/api/src/papers.ts:339`, `packages/provenance/src/recorder.ts:386`):

| site | what it delivers |
| --- | --- |
| `services/api/src/artifacts/materialize.ts` | Artifact promotion |
| `services/api/src/remote-runner.ts` | a pull landing in the local root |
| `services/api/src/agent-run/workspace-bindings.ts` | a committed workspace transfer |
| `services/api/src/subagents/index.ts` | the handoff's first observation of files it has not seen yet |

`services/api/src/subagents/index.ts:121` is untouched — that is a listing object, not a revision registration. In the handoff case a file that no longer exists in the live workspace is skipped rather than stamped with a time that is known to be wrong.

**The reconcile branch is deliberately unchanged.** `reconcileWorkspaceFiles` receives only `path`/`modifiedAt`/`size` and no digest, so it cannot tell a clock read a few milliseconds late from a real same-size edit. Inheriting `origin`/`contentHash`/`artifactVersionIds` there would credit that edit to the previous producer and break `services/api/src/store.test.ts:679` (*marks an unrecorded Workspace overwrite as unknown*, which requires `origin === "unknown"` and `revisions.length === 3`). An unrecorded external edit keeps degrading to `unknown`, and there is a case for that below so the trade cannot be lost silently.

## Verification

`services/api/src/artifacts/materialize.test.ts`, two new cases:

1. **`a promoted version keeps its attribution across the listing that follows`** — `materializeArtifact` → `listWorkspaceFiles` twice → `getWorkspaceFileProvenance`: `origin === "system"`, `contentHash === version.content.hash`, `artifactVersionIds === [version.id]`, **and** `lineage` and `artifacts` unchanged with no revision appended; then a second `materializeArtifact` of the identical bytes (the early-return branch) followed by another listing, still attributed.
2. **`a same-size edit on disk still degrades to unknown`** — the behaviour the fix must not trade away.

Both were run here through a scratch copy with the tag relaxed to `os:windows`, and I checked they actually pin the defect rather than passing vacuously: with the `materialize.ts` stamp reverted to `new Date()`, case 1 fails on `listing pass 1 must not replace the delivered revision`; with the fix it passes. The committed tags stay `os:linux`, so CI is what runs them as written.

`tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json` and `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` report nothing for these files. The suites that exercise `remote-runner` and the transfer commit end to end are `os:linux`-tagged and are skipped on this Windows host — CI runs those, and I am not claiming a local run of them.

1139.author: yuanzhou75
1139.body:
Closes #1132

## The defect

The Evolve LLM proxy wrote one usage row per proxied completion — correct — but keyed it by the **run**: `invocationId: evolve:<runId>` with `attemptIndex` held at `0`. The ledger's idempotency key is `(sessionId, invocationId, invocationKind, attemptIndex)`, so the first row was written and calls 2..N were absorbed as replays of call 1. The absorbing `return` is not an error, so the only warning on that path (`evolve_llm_usage_unrecorded`, gated on an exception) could not fire. Nothing anywhere said the spend had been dropped.

Measured on a real environment: a 73-call research recorded **0.83%** of its tokens, an 85-call one **0.93%**, and the surviving row's `totalTokens`/`startedAt`/`finishedAt` bracket only the first call — the row kept is call 1, relabelled as the run. `usageStatus: "reported"` on it asserts the provider figures were captured, which is what makes the error silent rather than merely coarse.

## The fix

**One identity per call** (`llm-proxy.ts`): `invocationId: evolve:<runId>:<randomUUID>`, keeping `invocationKind: "evolve"` and the row's `runId`. This is the shape `evolution/direction-draft.ts:58-60` already uses for the same `invocationKind`, and it is the option the issue ranks first: the alternative (a monotone `attemptIndex` per run) needs a durable counter. Cost still aggregates per run, because aggregation reads `runId`, not the key.

**The drop stops being silent** (`store.ts`): the suppressing branch now names the key it absorbed. The deduplication itself is untouched — `store.test.ts:1184` pins that an intentional replay of the same attempt must still be absorbed, and that is the behaviour the ledger depends on. What changed is that a writer keying distinct calls the same way can no longer look like correct idempotency.

## What the regression case pins

`services/api/src/evolution/llm-proxy.test.ts` — *every proxied completion of one run keeps its own ledger identity*: three proxied completions for one run must produce three **distinct ledger keys** with one shared `runId`, `sessionId` and `invocationKind`, and `attemptIndex` staying `0` (these are distinct calls, not retries, and inventing an attempt index would say otherwise). The assertion counts distinct keys rather than distinct `invocationId`s, because the key is what the real ledger deduplicates on.

I deliberately did **not** write §7.4 as literally worded ("N appends with the same run-scoped `invocationId` … must not collapse to one row"): that would require the ledger to distinguish rows by `id`, contradicting `store.test.ts:1184` and the contract in `model-usage.test.ts:83`. The call axis belongs to the writer, and that is where both the defect and the test sit.

Checked that the case fails for the right reason: with the run-scoped `invocationId` restored it fails on `each call carries its own ledger identity, so no call is read as a replay`.

## Verification

- `tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json` and `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json`: nothing for these files.
- `evolution/llm-proxy.test.ts` **18/18** and the `store.test.ts` dedup case pass here through a tag-relaxed copy — the latter while emitting the new `model_usage_append_deduplicated: task logical-call attempt 0 in session …` line, which is the observability part working.
- Both suites are tagged `os:linux`, so the committed files are what CI runs, not my relaxed copy.

## Not claimed

No backfill: calls 2..N are not recoverable from the ledger, as the issue states. I also did not change the `usageStatus` vocabulary, so a row still reports what the provider sent for that call.

1141.author: yuanzhou75
1141.body:
Relates #1133. This PR changes the recorder contract and the trajectory snapshot; the measured tool-only row class in #1133 is not restored here, so the issue stays open until its `need-human` question is answered.

## The defect

`AgentVersionRecorder` kept the link between a model call and the provider response it belongs to in **one mutable field** (`versioning.ts:156`). It was written synchronously by the event path (`response_start` → `:247`) and read *later, when the recording queue drained*, by `modelCompleted` (`:259`). `beforeTurn` (`:189`) and `afterAssembly` (`:215`) clear that field from inside the same queue, so a completion could be written after the next turn had already cleared it.

The report measured the consequence: **54 of 303** `model.completed` records carried no `responseId` although a `response_start` at the same turn had issued one; in the deterministic shape the recorder returned `turn: 2` and no id for a response `r1` that belonged to turn 1.

## The fix

- **The identity is data, not process state.** `modelCompleted(result, identity?)` takes `{ turn, responseId }`. A caller that sees `assistant.response.started` passes it; a supplied identity wins over the recorder's field, and `responseId: undefined` means *"this call has none"*, so a stale value is **dropped** instead of attributing the record to a neighbouring response (§7 of the report warned about exactly that mis-binding).
- **Without an explicit identity the evidence is snapshotted when the call completes**, not when the queue drains — the field is still valid at that moment in the built-in loop, whose `response_start` precedes the completion.
- **`JiuwenSwarmTrajectory` remembers the id it announced for the call** (`jiuwenswarm-trajectory.ts`) and passes it into the completion record; it is cleared when a new `modelRequest` starts, so the value handed to the record belongs to the call that just answered rather than to whatever the recorder happens to hold.

The recorder's field is still maintained for the evidence that other events carry (`assistant.response.started` itself, `state.committed`), so nothing else about the evidence shape changes.

## Verification

`services/api/src/native-agent/versioning.test.ts`, two new cases:

1. **`a completion record keeps the response id of the call it answers`** — `response_start r1 turn 1`, then a completion whose write is still queued while the next turn's `beforeTurn` clears the field. Asserts `responseId === "r1"` and `turn === 1`.
2. **`an identity passed by the caller wins over a recorder field that has moved on`** — the field has already advanced to turn 2; the caller passes `{ turn: 1, responseId: "r9" }` and the record carries exactly that.

**Mutation check:** reverting `modelCompleted` to read the evidence after `await this.pending` (the pre-fix ordering) turns **both** cases red with `actual: undefined`; with the fix they pass. `versioning.test.ts` 6/6, `jiuwenswarm-agent.test.ts`'s trajectory case still passes.

`tsc -p services/api --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` are clean. The two suites carry `os:linux`; their tags were relaxed for this Windows host and restored before pushing, so CI runs them as written. I did **not** re-run a live JiuwenSwarm session, so the 54/303 rate is not re-measured here — the fix is pinned by the deterministic cases above.

## Not changed on purpose

- The turn a completion records still comes from the recorder's counter when no identity is passed; the report classifies per-call turn drift as *structurally possible but not observable in the data*, and changing the turn contract needs the gateway to hand the call's turn back to the trajectory — a separate change.
- `reconcile`-style fallbacks in the trajectory server and the web timeline are untouched: they now simply receive an id where they previously guessed.

1143.author: yuanzhou75
1143.body:
Closes #1135.

## The defect

`scripts/start-stack.test.mjs::a leftover backup from a hard kill is restored on the next start` polled for the fixture file's **existence** and then read its **content**:

```js
`#!/bin/sh\ncat uv.lock > "${seenFile}"\nexit 0\n`   // :139
await waitFor(() => existsSync(seenFile), ...)         // :144
assert.equal(await readFile(seenFile, "utf8"), PRISTINE, ...)  // :145
```

The shell performs the `>` redirection — creating and truncating the target — **before** `cat` runs, so `existsSync` can return while the file is still zero bytes and the assertion reads `''`. That is the failure quoted in #1135 (`+ ''` vs `- 'version = 1\n# committed resolution\n'`), observed twice on the same head 13 minutes apart; a re-run did not clear it.

## The fix (test-only, both directions the issue suggested)

- **The polled path only ever appears complete.** The fake uv writes to `<seenFile>.tmp` and `mv`s it into place, so existence now implies completeness.
- **The wait is on the content the assertion wants**, so poll and assertion agree on what "the sync ran" means:
  `waitFor(async () => (await readFile(seenFile, "utf8").catch(() => "")) === PRISTINE, ...)`.
- **The same shape in the SIGTERM case is fixed too.** `echo $$ > uv.pid` has the identical truncate-before-write window; that case was safe only because the *next* wait reads `uv.lock` first. It now waits for a parseable pid. No assertion was relaxed, nothing was given a sleep, `PRISTINE` is untouched, and no case was skipped or re-tagged.

## Verification

The file carries `os:linux` and its fake `uv` is a POSIX shell script that the launcher spawns directly, so **it cannot execute on this Windows host** — the unmodified `main` version times out the same way (`timed out waiting for the fake uv to start` / `timed out waiting for the first sync to run`, ~30 s each), which is a host limitation, not this change.

What I could measure here is the mechanism itself, with a harness that recreates the fixture exactly (same `sh`, same redirection, same poll-then-read, 300 iterations each):

| synchronisation | incomplete reads |
| --- | --- |
| pre-fix: `existsSync` then read | **180 / 300** |
| fixed: tmp + `mv`, poll the content | **0 / 300** |

`sh -n` on the new fake-uv snippet is clean, so the shell change is valid POSIX. `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` reports nothing.

CI is what runs the real file as written; this PR is a **draft** and is not to be merged yet (`draft: true`, no auto-merge, not queued).

Relates #1133 (the issue stays open under `need-human` for the policy question it records).

## Why this is a follow-up

#1141 landed the per-call binding: a caller that sees `assistant.response.started` passes the id, and a completion whose write is still queued no longer loses an id that had already been issued. HongyeZhou then pointed out the class it does not cover: **a call with no text and no reasoning gets its response opened by the adapter after the completion has been requested** (`services/adapter/src/sciencediscovery_adapter/events.py:152-162`), so no caller can pass that id — and the first cut deleted the recorder's value whenever an identity was supplied, leaving exactly the tool-only rows anonymous.

## What changed

- `completedEvidence` takes the caller's id when it has one, and otherwise falls back to the recorder's value **only when that value was announced for the same turn**. The recorder now remembers which turn its `responseId` belongs to (`responseIdTurn`), set with the id and cleared at both existing clearing points.
- The completion write therefore picks up an id minted after it was requested, while a leftover from a neighbouring turn is still never attributed to this record — "dropped" cannot silently become "mis-bound".
- `modelCompleted` keeps the call-time snapshot for callers that supply no identity at all (the built-in loop, whose `response_start` already arrived), and re-reads at write time only for the late-mint case.

## Verification

`services/api/src/native-agent/versioning.test.ts` 8/8 with the tag relaxed for this Windows host and restored before pushing:

- a response id minted **after** the completion was requested still reaches the record (`late-1`);
- an id belonging to **another turn** is never reused for this record;
- the two cases #1141 added still pass (queued write surviving the next turn's clearing; a supplied identity winning over a moved-on field).

Mutation checks, both red before the fix and green after: removing the fallback turns the late-id case red (`actual: undefined`); reading the evidence after the queue drain turns the first case red. `tsc -p services/api` and `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` are clean.

## Residual (stated, not closed)

The fallback restores parity with main before #1141: it reads at the point the completion write drains, now guarded by the turn the id was announced for. It does **not** move that read past the moment the tool-only rows lost the id — the adapter mints those ids in another process and channel, and nothing orders that mint against the recorder's drain. So the class is restored **only when the mint beats the drain**; the rest stays for the backfill/bounded-wait/§7.2 choice #1133 keeps under 
eed-human.

The late-id test pins the favourable ordering (an id announced between the call and the write), not a real adapter mint landing inside that window; that is what the test can assert without a live swarm instance.

Known cosmetic: this comment line carries one stray CR where the backtick before "responseId" belongs (ersioning.ts:157) — comment text only, fixed in the next change to this file rather than in another review cycle here.

1148.body:
Relates #1140 — items 7.1, 7.2, 7.4 and 7.5 land here; 7.3 is dropped and argued on the issue

## What the user sees today, and what changes

A long-trajectory session's dialog showed three false things at once: a raw browser string (`signal is aborted without reason`), a claim that the session had no workspace files while it had 176, and two disabled export buttons. None of that was a server error — the preview was merely slow, and the caller had left.

**1. The dialog recognises its own cancellation.** `export-preview-cache.ts` aborted with no reason, so Chromium manufactured that string and `errorText` rendered it verbatim. It now aborts with `PreviewBudgetExpired` (name `AbortError`, so the existing `isAbortError` in `apps/web/src/api/client.ts` matches), and the dialog turns that — and the server's existing `EXPORT_PREVIEW_PENDING` answer — into a localized "still preparing, it retries automatically" status line instead of an error.

**2. "Not determined" is no longer rendered as "empty".** The empty state was `!files.length ? noWorkspaceFiles : null`, true for a preview that had not arrived. It now speaks only for a successful preview. Two new keys, both locales.

**3. A slow preview is served by later polls, not by a timer.** The route still holds the request open for as long as the work takes; what is truthful now is the client side of it — the dialog names its own 10 s cancellation and shows the retrying state instead of a browser string, and its 3 s poll picks the result up when the server finishes. No wall-clock budget is imposed on `defaults()`: an earlier revision of this branch added one and it answered 202 to a fixture that legitimately needs ~49 s, because a clock cannot tell "slow but finishing" from "pathological". A pending-for-slow rule has to key off queue starvation rather than elapsed time, and that is not in this PR (see the issue's §7.3).

**4. One session's dialog no longer waits behind another's.** The service had a single serial chain for every project and session; it is now one chain per `projectId:sessionId`. Ordering *within* a session — and the deadlock hazard the code warns about — is unchanged, and `close()` drains every chain.

**5. §7.4: one closure walk per revision, not one per profile.** Two of the five profiles carry the full trajectory and each hydrated the same 3.2 GB / 7 740-object closure independently. The sizing pass records what the walk produced, keyed by **walk shape and session** (`full:` / `summary:`) and by evidence revision: one byte count, the CAS hashes and the version refs per entry, in order. The second full-trajectory profile replays those numbers instead of re-reading the records, and a summarized walk can never feed a full one. The replay reproduces `estimatedBytes` exactly, including the comma accounting, which depends on entry order. Only measurements are cached, never a detail object: #1085 was lost to keeping entries alive.

## What this does not do

- **§7.3 (make "slow" answer like "busy")** is deliberately dropped — see above and the comment on the issue.
- **§7.6 (sizing without deserialising)** is **not done**, and I had its premise wrong in an earlier revision of this description: I wrote that the preview path contains no `readRecord`, on the strength of `research-snapshots.ts` alone. It does — `packages/trajectory/src/server.ts:69` (`await store.readRecord(ref, kind)`) and `:312` (`await store.readRecord(event.payloadRef)`) resolve every trajectory detail the walk asks for, so each entry the preview sizes is a record read plus a JSON parse. That is what §7.4 above removes half of, and it is why the issue's cost model holds. What remains for §7.6 proper is reading only the dependency list instead of deserialising whole records, which is a change of its own.
- **§7.7 / §7.8** are untouched.

## Rendered evidence for the two new states

Both locales, before and after, of the export dialog. These are renderer-level
captures: the component's markup with the app's own `tokens.css` / `base.css` /
`primitives.css` / `dialogs.css` and the real `messages.ts` strings, rendered in
Chromium. They are not Electron-window captures and not a live interaction.

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| en | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1148/docs/screenshots/1148/1148-en-before.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1148/docs/screenshots/1148/1148-en-after.png) |
| zh | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1148/docs/screenshots/1148/1148-zh-before.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1148/docs/screenshots/1148/1148-zh-after.png) |

**before** is today's behaviour: the status line carries Chromium's own
`signal is aborted without reason`, and the custom-content section claims the
session has no workspace files. **after** is this branch: a localized "still
preparing, it retries automatically" status line, and "the export scope has not
been determined yet" instead of an empty claim.

That the stylesheet is actually applied was checked rather than assumed, since a
capture with no styles looks plausible until someone reads it: a headless probe
over the same document reports `.research-export-dialog` at `width: 620px`
(matching `dialogs.css`), `display: flex`, background `rgb(255,255,255)`, heading
ink `rgb(52, 64, 84)` and the selected card's border `rgb(154, 184, 236)` — i.e.
the theme tokens resolved.

**One limit I am stating plainly:** I cannot view images, so this is a
programmatic check of layout and tokens plus the exact strings from `messages.ts`,
not an eye check. The wording decisions are the reviewers' and the user's to
accept; the author approval is still pending and this PR should not be read as
claiming otherwise.

## Verification

- `tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json` and `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json`: clean for every file this PR touches. (The three `evolution/proposal.ts` errors are this checkout's stale schema and are present without these changes; to make the check meaningful I also synced `memory-watch.ts`, `heap-budget.ts` and `trajectory.ts` from `main`, which this tree was missing.)
- `tsc` over `apps/web` scoped to the two changed files: clean.
- CI on head `1ac9ee256bb6`: `UT`, `merge-gate`, `L1`, `ST`, `Coverage`, `Docker image`, both `Binary release`s and `CodeCheck` all pass, no red, nothing skipped that matters.
- The existing serialization assertions still hold by construction: the chain is per session, so one dialog's five profiles still run one at a time (`peak === 1`), and a second `get()` for the same session joins the same chain.
- **New regression case** (`services/api/src/research-preview-trajectory-replay.test.ts`, new file, no existing fixture touched): seeding `full:<sessionId>` with a number no empty session's real walk can produce shows the replay branch reads the map; an empty cache adds nothing and must still gain the `full:<sessionId>` key, which pins the **write** — the defect both reviewers caught; a `summary:<sessionId>` entry is ignored by a full walk, pinning the shape key. The same file also covers the replay branch's own omission push and the receipt's bound: a seeded `full:<sessionId>` entry that names an unreadable record has to reappear in `omissions` when a later profile replays that walk (deleting the replay push at `research-snapshots.ts:441` turns the case red), and a seeded list two past `TRAJECTORY_OMISSION_LIMIT` makes the receipt name exactly five entries and report the two it withheld (disabling the overflow line at `:485` turns that case red). Boundary, stated narrowly: this proves the replay reads and the walk writes that map; it does **not** observe `readTrajectoryDetail` not being called, because that closure is not exported.
- **Unreadable-record omission** (`research-preview-trajectory-replay.test.ts`): one `agent.record` stream event whose `payloadRef` names an object that was never written makes the lazy loader throw for that entry only, and the case asserts the **session-scoped prefix** `trajectory:<sessionId>:` reaches the returned `omissions` — it does not pin the entry id. The two seeded cases above do pin exact strings, because those strings are the test's own. It drives the export path (the first walk, `:458`); the replaying profile's own push at `:441` is the seeded case above, which is the part the export case cannot reach.
- **Rendered evidence** for the two new states is in the section above: both locales, before and after, with the programmatic check that the stylesheet and theme tokens actually applied.

1153.body:
Relates #1133 — the deterministic-id half of it. The issue's second `need-human` item is "where the response id is minted", and this takes option (a): at the model-call boundary. It stays `Relates` because closing the issue should also show one measured run where no completion is anonymous, and this host cannot produce that run (the adapter runtime is not installed here), so the issue is left to close on that evidence rather than on this claim.

## Why the previous two attempts could not close it

#1141 bound the id per call and #1145 made a *late* id reusable by its own turn, but both still needed the adapter to announce first. For a turn that answers with only a tool call there is nothing to announce until Swarm has received the tool call, which is after this side has already written the record:

- the gateway streams the `tool_calls` frame (`services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts:556`) and then writes `model.completed` (`:558`);
- the adapter opens the response only when Swarm replays it as `chat.tool_call` (`services/adapter/src/sciencediscovery_adapter/events.py:152-162`, `:232-264`), minting a fresh `uuid4` there.

Two processes, two streams, no ordering. That is why #1145 had to state its residual as "restored only when the mint beats the drain".

## What changed

- **The call is an object, not a value.** The gateway mints `call = { responseId }` for every task call before the request leaves, passes it into `request(...)` so the queued `model_request` binds that call to the turn it opens, and passes it back into `completed(...)`. `modelCompleted` reads its own identity and its own turn; nothing shared is read across calls, so dispatch A → dispatch B → complete A cannot stamp A with B's id or B's turn. Housekeeping is not recorded, so it never gets an identity.
- **The id travels back with the response** in `x-sciencediscovery-response-id`, on the streaming and the JSON response.
- **The adapter's proxy keeps it** (`llm_proxy.py`): the header is stripped before the response is forwarded on to Swarm — Swarm has no use for it — and queued on the run's route, oldest first.
- **The mapper claims it** (`events.py::_open_response`) when it announces that response. A Swarm pointed at something other than this run's gateway dispatches no id and keeps the locally minted uuid, unchanged.
- **A stale adapter is *best-effort* visible.** The recorder remembers the id each turn's `model.completed` was written with, and compares an announcement against it — but only when that announcement is the last record still outstanding for the run, because with another call in flight the announcement may belong to that one and a false alarm sends an operator after a swap that did not happen. Two cases are therefore **not** compared: an announcement that arrives after the next call has already opened, and any mismatch that arrives while a stale entry is still waiting. The id on the record itself never depends on this comparison.

## Verification

- `tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit`: clean.
- `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.test.ts`: **63 / 64**. The one failure asserts `stat().mode & 0o777 === 0o600`, a Unix permission Windows cannot express; it fails the same way with this change reverted.
- `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.test.ts`: **117 / 118**. The one failure expects `/data/skill-snapshots/...` but Windows yields `\data\skill-snapshots\...`; both files were run with the `os` tag relaxed to this host and restored before pushing.
- New cases:
  - the id is settled **before** the streamer runs, equals the header the adapter receives, and is the identity the completion is recorded under;
  - a housekeeping call carries no header and is never named;
  - **interleaving**: dispatch A, dispatch B, then complete A and B → `[[turn 0, id-a], [turn 1, id-b]]`, each call keeping its own id and turn;
  - **stale adapter**: a call recorded as `recorded-id`, then an announcement of `adapter-own` → the warning names both;
  - the fake adapter echoes the header value as the id it announces, so the record id and the event id are asserted to be the same value end to end.
- **The adapter pytest suite was not run by me here**: `fastapi` is not installed on this host, so `test_events.py` and `test_llm_proxy.py` (two new cases each) are the CI's to run. The review bot ran them on a clean tree at this content (`test_llm_proxy.py`, `test_events.py`, `test_agent_runs.py`: 163 passed).

## Deployment note

API and adapter agree on the id through one header and ship from one repository. With an older adapter the record is still named while the announced event carries the adapter's own uuid; that mismatch is logged when the announcement is the only outstanding one, and stays quiet otherwise.

## Not changed

- The built-in runtime keeps its own path: `completedEvidence`'s turn guard and its fallback to the recorder's field are untouched, and remain the fallback when a call arrives without an identity.
- `callTurns` entries for a call that never completes are not pruned. Pruning by turn would drop the entry of a call still in flight and reintroduce the swap; a failure hook on the observer is the right shape and is not added here.
- The stale-adapter diagnostic is not keyed on the turn the adapter announced. That is the right shape and is filed as a follow-up rather than patched inside this branch: it needs proof that the adapter's turn counter and the trajectory's agree on every path, and a wrong key would turn a silent miss into a wrong warning.
- No live JiuwenSwarm run was re-measured, so the 54/303 rate is not re-derived; the fix is pinned by the ordering, interleaving and stale-adapter tests above.
